# ui::DecimalFormatter

Header: `winui/core/NumberFormat.hpp`.

Formats and parses plain decimal numbers.

A plain value handed to [NumberBoxControl::set_number_formatter()](../controls/number-box.md#set_number_formatter) or [ui::NumberBox::number_formatter](../controls/number-box.md#uinumberbox-number_formatter). Unless [`symbols`](#symbols) pins them, the separators follow the regional format at the time of each call, so the same formatter writes "1,5" in de-DE and "1.5" in en-US.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::DecimalFormatter dollars;
dollars.fraction_digits = 2;
dollars.rounder         = ui::IncrementNumberRounder{0.01, ui::RoundingAlgorithm::RoundHalfUp};

// The NumberBox shows 3 as "3.00" and reads what the user types back with the same formatter.
ui::Property<std::optional<double>> price{3.0};
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .spacing = 8,
    .content = {
        ui::NumberBox{.header = "Price", .value = price, .min = 0.0, .number_formatter = dollars},
        ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(price, [dollars](const std::optional<double>& p) {
            return p ? "Three for $" + dollars.format(*p * 3.0) : std::string{};
        })},
    },
});

// Text from elsewhere, a CSV cell say, parses the same way; nullopt when it is not a number.
const std::optional<double> cell = dollars.parse(" 4.5 "); // 4.5
```

## integer_digits

```cpp
int integer_digits = 1
```

The fewest integer digits shown, padded with leading zeros.

## fraction_digits

```cpp
int fraction_digits = 0
```

The fewest fraction digits shown, padded with trailing zeros. More are shown when the value has them. Set [`rounder`](#rounder) to limit them.

## is_grouped

```cpp
bool is_grouped = false
```

Groups the integer digits with the grouping separator, by default in threes with `,`.

## is_decimal_point_always_displayed

```cpp
bool is_decimal_point_always_displayed = false
```

Shows the decimal point even with no fraction digits.

## rounder

```cpp
std::optional<IncrementNumberRounder> rounder {}
```

Rounds the value before formatting; unset formats it unrounded.

## symbols

```cpp
std::optional<NumberFormatSymbols> symbols {}
```

The separators. Unset follows [regional_number_format()](namespace-ui.md#regional_number_format), the user's locale. [NumberFormatSymbols::invariant()](number-format-symbols.md#invariant) pins `.` and `,`.

## effective_symbols

```cpp
const NumberFormatSymbols& effective_symbols() const
```

The separators this formatter writes and reads with: [`symbols`](#symbols), or the regional format.

## format

```cpp
std::string format(double value) const
```

`value` as text. NaN and the infinities format as "NaN", "∞" and "-∞".

## parse

```cpp
std::optional<double> parse(std::string_view text) const
```

Reads the whole of `text`, surrounding spaces aside, as one number written with the decimal separator. Grouping separators are allowed when [`is_grouped`](#is_grouped) is set. Returns nullopt when `text` is not a number.
